title: Climate Analog Search Tools
text: analogs package provides fast, flexible tools climate analog analyses. efficiently searches large reference datasets find locations best match query sites based climate similarity geographic proximity.

title: Climate Analog Search Tools
text: package supports range analyses. core workhorse function analog_search(). Common query types supported via dedicated helper functions: analog_velocity() finds k nearest geographic analogs hard climate constraint analog_similarity() finds k nearest climate analogs within geographic constraint analog_availability() counts analogs meet climate distance thresholds analog_intensity() computes distance-weighted aggregations analog properties Geographic distance computations support projected coordinates well lon-lat coordinates via great circle distances. Multivariate climate distances Euclidean default, can use mahalanobis_transform() implement Mahalanobis distance based global spatial covariance, supply x_cov analog_*() function account site-specific climate covariance patterns.

title: Climate Analog Search Tools
text: analogs uses optimized C++ algorithms parallel processing handle computationally intensive pairwise distance calculations across millions locations. package built around lattice search index. functions sufficient many analyses, optimization possible using build_analog_index() pre-build reusable search index, using tune_index_res() find optimal index parameters specific data.

title: Analog availability: count of all analogs within climate/geographic limits — analog_availability
text: Return type depends input format query mode. Returns data.frame, unless x SpatRaster results exactly one record per input cell (aggregation mode, pairwise k = 1), case returns SpatRaster one layer per output variable. Pairwise mode (stat = NULL "none") returns one row per focal-analog pair, following variables: index, x, y: Focal location (1-based index coordinates) corresponding input x analog_index, analog_x, analog_y: Analog location corresponding input pool clim_dist: Climate distance (Euclidean Mahalanobis) geog_dist: Geographic distance (km lonlat, projection units otherwise) Value columns (values provided): one per variable Aggregation mode (one stat values) returns one row per focal location, following variables: index, x, y: Focal location One column per requested statistic. stat single values variable: column named stat (e.g., sum, mean). stat multiple values variables: columns named {stat}_{varname} (e.g., sum_biomass, mean_richness) results include metadata attributes (select, stat, weight, etc.). text: x Focal locations analogs found. matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables, SpatRaster climate variable layers. pool reference dataset search analogs. Radius units specified kilometers coord_type = "lonlat", projected coordinate units coord_type = "projected". weight Weighting function matches, used stat includes "sum_weights" "mean_weights". One : "uniform": matches weighted equally (weight = 1.0). "inverse_clim": Inverse climate distance, weight = 1 / (climate_distance + eps), epsilon given theta. "inverse_geog": Inverse geographic distance, weight = 1 / (geographic_distance + eps), epsilon given theta. "gaussian_clim": Gaussian kernel climate distance, weight = exp(-climate_distance^2 / (2sigma^2)), sigma given theta.  "gaussian_geog": Gaussian kernel geographic distance, weight = exp(-geographic_distance^2 / (2sigma^2)), sigma given theta. Interpretation depends weight: "inverse_clim" "inverse_geog": epsilon value added distances (scalar; default: 1e-12 climate, 1e-6 geography). "gaussian_clim" "gaussian_geog": sigma bandwidth parameter (scalar; larger values = slower decay distance). "gaussian_joint": 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog) giving bandwidths climate geographic dimensions. title: Find Climate Analogs — analog_search
text: Parameters fall four categories: Data parameters (x, pool, x_cov, values, coord_type) give attributes data operate. Selection parameters (select, max_clim, max_geog, k) define analogs select pool x. Aggregation parameters (stat, weight, theta) control selected analogs summarized. Computation parameters (index_res, n_threads) specify internal behavior affecting compute performance. function uses spatial indexing structure (lattice-based) quickly search large reference datasets. Climate similarity measured using Euclidean distance climate space (ideally pre-whitened). Geographic distance can computed lon/lat coordinates (great-circle distance) projected coordinates (planar distance).

title: Find Climate Analogs — analog_search
code: if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{ # Basic pair queries analog_search(x = focal, pool = ref, select = "all", max_clim = 0.5) analog_search(x = focal, pool = ref, select = "knn_geog", max_clim = 0.5, k = 1)  # Single aggregation analog_search(x = focal, pool = ref, select = "all", stat = "count", max_clim = 0.5)  # Multiple aggregations in one pass analog_search(x = focal, pool = ref, select = "all",               stat = c("count", "sum_weights", "mean_weights"),               max_clim = 0.5, weight = "gaussian_clim", theta = 0.1)  # With pre-built index (for repeated queries) index <- build_analog_index(ref) analog_search(x = focal1, pool = index, select = "knn_geog", max_clim = 0.5, k = 1) analog_search(x = focal2, pool = index, select = "all", stat = "count", max_clim = 0.3) } # }  # With user-defined values values_df <- data.frame(   biomass = runif(nrow(ref), 0, 100),   richness = rpois(nrow(ref), 20) ) #> Error: object 'ref' not found  analog_search(x = focal, pool = ref, values = values_df,               stat = c("count", "sum", "mean"),               max_clim = 0.5) #> Error: object 'ref' not found # Returns: index, x, y, count, sum_biomass, mean_biomass, sum_richness, mean_richness  # Weighted aggregation of values analog_search(x = focal, pool = ref, values = values_df$biomass,               stat = c("weighted_sum", "weighted_mean"),               weight = "gaussian_clim", theta = 0.2,               max_clim = 0.5) #> Error: object 'ref' not found # Returns: index, x, y, weighted_sum, weighted_mean

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res
text: x Focal locations analogs found. matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables, SpatRaster climate variable layers. pool reference dataset search analogs. Either: Matrix/data.frame columns x, y, climate variables, SpatRaster climate variable layers, analog_index() object created build_analog_index() (repeated queries). select Character string specifying analog selection strategy. One : "" (default): Select analogs satisfy max_clim max_geog constraints. "knn_clim": focal, select k analogs smallest climate distance, subject filters. "knn_geog": focal, select k analogs smallest geographic distance, subject filters. stat Statistic(s) used aggregate selected analogs. Either: NULL "none": Return selected analog pairs data.frame. "count": focal, count number selected analogs. "sum_weights": focal, sum weights selected analogs (see weight theta). "mean_weights": focal, mean weights selected analogs. "sum": Sum values across analogs (requires values). "mean": Mean values across analogs (requires values). "weighted_sum": Sum (value × weight) across analogs (requires values weight). "weighted_mean": Weighted mean values across analogs (requires values weight). character vector combining multiple stats (e.g., c("count", "sum", "mean")). Note: "none" combined stats. max_clim Maximum climate distance constraint (default: NULL = climate constraint). Can either: scalar: Euclidean radius climate space (e.g., 0.5) vector: Per-variable absolute differences (length must equal number climate variables) reference locations within climate distance considered. x_cov provided, scalar thresholds interpreted Mahalanobis distance units. max_geog Maximum geographic distance constraint (default: NULL = geographic constraint). specified, reference locations within distance considered. Radius units specified kilometers coord_type = "lonlat", projected coordinate units coord_type = "projected". k Number nearest analogs return per focal location kNN selection modes. Required select "knn_geog" "knn_clim"; must NULL select = "". weight Weighting function matches, used stat includes "sum_weights" "mean_weights". One : "uniform": matches weighted equally (weight = 1.0). "inverse_clim": Inverse climate distance, weight = 1 / (climate_distance + eps), epsilon given theta. "inverse_geog": Inverse geographic distance, weight = 1 / (geographic_distance + eps), epsilon given theta. "gaussian_clim": Gaussian kernel climate distance, weight = exp(-climate_distance^2 / (2sigma^2)), sigma given theta.  "gaussian_geog": Gaussian kernel geographic distance, weight = exp(-geographic_distance^2 / (2sigma^2)), sigma given theta. "gaussian_joint": Joint Gaussian kernel, weight = exp(-climate_distance^2/(2sigma_c^2) - geographic_distance^2/(2sigma_g^2)), sigma values given theta 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog). "inverse_joint": Joint inverse distance, weight = 1 / sqrt((climate_distance + eps_clim)^2 + (geographic_distance + eps_geog)^2), epsilon values given theta 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog). stat including weighted aggregations, weight must NULL. theta Optional numeric parameter used weighting functions stat includes "sum_weights" "mean_weights" weight "uniform". Interpretation depends weight: "inverse_clim" "inverse_geog": epsilon value added distances (scalar; default: 1e-12 climate, 1e-6 geography). "gaussian_clim" "gaussian_geog": sigma bandwidth parameter (scalar; larger values = slower decay distance). "gaussian_joint": 2-element vector c(sigma_clim, sigma_geog) giving bandwidths climate geographic dimensions. "inverse_joint": 2-element vector c(eps_clim, eps_geog) giving epsilon values climate geographic dimensions. theta NULL, sensible defaults used single-parameter weights. weight = "uniform" non-weighted aggregations, theta must NULL. x_cov Optional focal-specific covariance matrices Mahalanobis distance calculations. matrix data.frame one row per focal location one column per unique covariance component. n climate variables, n*(n+1)/2 unique components, ordered : variances first (diagonals), covariances (upper triangle row). values Optional user-defined variables reference location aggregate across selected analogs. Can : numeric vector (single variable) matrix data.frame numeric columns (multiple variables) Must exactly nrow(pool) rows (number reference locations pool index). row corresponds reference location. provided, enables value-based aggregation stats: "sum": Sum values across analogs "mean": Mean values across analogs "weighted_sum": Sum (value × weight) - requires weight "weighted_mean": Sum (value × weight) / sum weights - requires weight stat = NULL/"none" (pairs mode), value columns included output analog pair. coord_type Coordinate system type: "auto" (default): Automatically detect coordinate ranges. "lonlat": Unprojected lon/lat coordinates (uses great-circle distance; assumes max_geog km). "projected": Projected XY coordinates (uses planar distance; assumes max_geog projection units). n_threads Optional integer number threads use computation. NULL (default), global RcppParallel setting used (see RcppParallel::setThreadOptions). default_res Default resolution use starting point search. Default 16. verbose Logical; TRUE, print selected resolution. Default FALSE.

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res

title: Tune Index Resolution — tune_index_res
text: function uses adaptive bracketing algorithm: Starts three resolutions: default/2, default, default*2 Evaluates elapsed time minimum edge, expands search direction Returns resolution lowest elapsed time typically requires 3-5 query evaluations total, making much faster exhaustive grid search. function performs tuning non-trivial problem sizes (>2000 focal points). smaller datasets, returns default resolution. subsample focal points used benchmarking keep tuning fast still representative actual query performance.
